narrative.overview:
The site reads like a developer's screen after hours: near-black, set entirely in a monospace face, quiet, and a little wry. The studio's whole pitch is that you talk to the people who write the code, so the interface looks like where that code gets written. Section labels are code comments, the hero carries a shell-script joke, and a field of slow, faint stars drifts behind everything, nudged toward the cursor.

Density is calm and editorial rather than dashboard-tight: one column of sections, generous vertical gaps, short measure for prose, and cards that sit on the stars as translucent glass instead of opaque panels. Color is almost absent. The only hue on the page is a single blue-to-cyan light sweep that crosses the wordmark once on load; project screenshots carry the rest of the color.

Dark is the canonical theme and the default. A light theme exists via the toggle but is secondary and not yet tuned; design and review against dark first.
keyCharacteristics: Monospace everywhere: JetBrains Mono for display, headings, body and labels.
Strict grayscale UI on a near-black canvas; color only from the logo shine and real screenshots.
Translucent glass cards (30% slate, backdrop blur, hairline ring) floating over a star field.
Developer-flavoured microcopy as ornament: // label, numbered 01 steps, tabular stats.
Motion that settles once: staggered blur-in entrance, a single shine sweep, scroll reveals that move but never fade. All gated by prefers-reduced-motion.

rules.name: The Monochrome Rule
rules.body: UI chrome is grayscale. Hierarchy comes from lightness (paper → fog → slate), never from hue. If a new element seems to need a color, it needs contrast or size instead.

rules.name: The One Spark Rule
rules.body: The blue-cyan shine appears once per page, on the wordmark, and plays once. A second spark makes it decoration instead of a signature.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Everything is JetBrains Mono. Hierarchy is size, weight, tracking and lightness; never introduce a second display or body face.

rules.name: The Comment Label Rule
rules.body: Every section opens with a lowercase-in-copy, uppercase-rendered // label above its headline. It's the system's signature; don't drop it or swap it for an eyebrow pill.

rules.name: The Glass Over Stars Rule
rules.body: Surfaces that sit on the page are translucent (slate 30% + blur + hairline), never opaque fills. The stars must stay faintly visible through every card.

dos: Do design and review in dark mode first; it is the default and the reference.
Do set every new piece of text in JetBrains Mono and build hierarchy from size, weight (400–700), tracking and lightness.
Do open every section with the SectionHeader (// label + headline), left-aligned.
Do put content surfaces on glass: slate at 30%, backdrop blur, 1px hairline, 24px corners, through shadcn `Card`.

Do gate every animation behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and make content fully visible without JS (CSS reveals move content 32px, they never fade it, so text never fails contrast mid-animation).
Do keep prose to a max width of 42rem and supporting text in fog.
donts: Don't add hue to UI chrome: no colored buttons, links, borders, icon tints or section backgrounds (The Monochrome Rule).
Don't reuse the blue-cyan shine anywhere but the hero wordmark, or let it loop (The One Spark Rule).
Don't introduce a second typeface, including Inter, which is installed but intentionally unused.
Don't make surfaces opaque over the star field, or stack heavy drop shadows; depth is translucency.
Don't center-align section headers or the hero.
Don't treat the current light theme as a reference; its glass cards turn flat grey and need their own pass before light mode is designed against.
